title: Welcome and Table of Contents
summary: What SS1 Mathematics Second Term covers (geometry and trigonometry), how to use the notes, and a map of every unit.

p: Welcome back. In First Term you worked with numbers, algebra and logic. In Second Term the main subject is geometry and trigonometry. You will draw exact shapes with a ruler and compasses, study the paths of moving points (loci), prove important theorems about triangles and parallel lines, and meet trigonometry, which links angles and lengths and is used by engineers, pilots and surveyors.
Geometry needs a sharp pencil, a ruler, compasses, a protractor (for checking) and a clean page. Many questions in WAEC and NECO ask you to draw, so practise often.

Read each unit slowly and look at every picture. When there is a construction, copy it on paper with your own tools, step by step. Do the activity at the end of each unit. Then do the practice questions. They do not count towards a mark; they help you check your understanding. Answer them all correctly to complete the unit.
The midterm examination falls in Week 5 and there is a break in Week 7, so there are no new units for those weeks. Use them to revise.

p: Always draw a clear diagram and label it. In constructions, do not rub out your arcs. In riders, write a reason for every step. In trigonometry, label the sides (opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse) before you choose a ratio, and make sure your calculator is in degree mode.

activity: Check that you have a ruler, a pair of compasses, a protractor and a sharp pencil. Draw a straight line and a circle with your compasses to test them.
